_comment_name: HK Grotesk is what this typeface was called before it was renamed,
and it is still the name people ask for it by. It is not the name
the file answers to: the name table inside HankenGrotesk-Italic.ttf
says 'Hanken Grotesk', and the name table is the only thing Windows
and local() key on. So the pack is declared under what the file says
and the old name is written down here, once, so the next person
looking for HK Grotesk finds it.
_comment_family: The block face of fitness-story, whose picked words are set in
hanken-grotesk-semibolditalic beside it. Both cuts lean — the slant
is the show's, not the highlight's — so the two are told apart by
weight alone, 400 against 600, and a swap between them is not a
different look, it is the highlight disappearing into the text.
The full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
telegraf-ultralight declares 'Telegraf UltraLight' rather than
'Telegraf'. ID 1 on this file is the bare 'Hanken Grotesk', which any
upright cut of the family installed on the machine would answer to,
and a block that came back upright is a block set in the wrong face.
Two distinct family names is also what lets one channel be set in
both at once, because fontguard keys its check by family and each cut
is then verified in its own right.
Weight 400, which is what the file's OS/2 table says. This family's
italic is a slant and not a weight, and asking for anything else
invites a browser to synthesise a difference the file does not have.
Registered at style normal on purpose, the same way rift is. The
slant is drawn into the letterforms; declaring the face italic as
well would leave the canvas — which asks for normal — either missing
it or being handed a synthetic oblique of something else. Normal
means 'this file, as drawn'.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.

_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied: most of the faces in
this folder fall back through Impact and Arial Black because most of
them are heavy display cuts, and this is not one. It is a 400-weight
grotesque set at caption size, and Segoe UI is the nearest thing to
that every Windows this app runs on is certain to have. It comes out
upright, because the face is registered at style normal and there is
nothing left to slant it — which is a title in the wrong face either
way, and fontguard is what stops one being drawn.
